metadata.note: Public-facing recreation infrastructure with activity/service lists, operations, fees, seasons, permits, restrictions, water/restrooms, and directions when published.

properties.recarea_description: What was once an old railroad bed just down the road from the town of Deary, Idaho, is now the delightful Potlatch Canyon hiking trail.  This trail is an amazing place to experience colorful wildflower displays, take in views overlooking the canyon, stroll in and out of the shadows created by towering cedar trees and ponderosa pines and experience the panoramic views awaiting you in wide open meadows--you might even catch a glimpse of a moose!
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.operational_hours: Day use only; no overnight camping allowed
properties.directions: From Deary, Idaho head east on Highway 8 to the town of Helmer. In Helmer follow signs to Little Boulder Campground (right on Park Road). After three miles trailhead is on your left just before bridge.

properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site

properties.recarea_description: The Upper Bear Summit Trailhead has a loading/unloading ramp for animals and serves Bear Summit (#286) and Bear Summit West (#288) trails.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
No fees are required for this site
properties.operational_hours: Day use only; no overnight camping allowed

properties.recarea_description: Forty-six miles northeast of Lowell, at milepost 143 along the Northwest Passage Scenic Byway and All American Road (US Highway 12), visitors can witness the magnificent Mocus Point suspension bridge leading into the Selway Bitterroot Wilderness across the Lochsa River. Spacious parking, hitchrails, stock ramps and a restroom provide for a comfortable unloading zone whether you are stopped for a break from your drive or preparing for a long pack trip into the wilderness.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: From Lowell, ID, drive 46 miles northeast on US Hwy 12 to milepost 143.

properties.activity_type_list: FISHING, RIVER / STREAM | HORSEBACK RIDING | MOTORCYCLES & SCOOTERS
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.operational_hours: Day use only; no overnight camping allowed

properties.recarea_description: This trailhead is part of the Ridge To Rivers Trail System.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.operational_hours: June - End of September Unless closed by snow
properties.directions: From Boise take 8th street north to the trailhead

properties.recarea_description: This trail is locally known as the Pole Canyon Trail.  Just South of Victor, ID, the Allen Canyon-Pole Canyon Trail (014) is a popular destition for local motorbikes, horseback riders, hikers, and mountain bikers.  A prolonged uphill grade make this trail a challenge for hikers and mountain bikers alike and steep rocky sections of trail on the Western leg of the 014 horseshoe provide for expert level technical challenge.  The entire trail can be used as a loop by combining the 014 with a small section of the Powerline Trail (031).  Pole Canyon usually receives a moderate to high amount of use in summer evenings and weekends.  Please follow all rules concerning Trail Right-Of-Way.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.operational_hours: Day use only: open sunrise to sunset
properties.directions: From Victor, ID head South on Continue onto Forest Rd 60547/Pole Canyon Rd

properties.recarea_description: This is the trailhead for trail #4153, Fanny's Hole and #4152, Buster Lake Trail.  There is one campsite above Buster Lake available for overnight camping.  The road is narrow and steep; 4wd recommended.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: From Challis, Idaho head west on Yankee Fork Rd/Main St and continue for 5 miles. Then turn left onto Garden Creek Rd. Stay on Garden Cr Rd for a little over 7 miles, trailhead will be at the end of the road.

properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site

properties.recarea_description: Located on the North side of the East Fork South Fork Salmon River Road NFSR #51887. TH is signed and has a registration box. Parking availability for up to 10 vehicles.

This trailhead has minimal development, providing access to #4197, Merriam Lake, #4089 Leatherman Pass, and #4198 Pass Lake trails. One metal fire ring, a picnic table and a two-sided latrine are on site.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: From Mackay drive north on US-93 N for about 22 miles. Turn right onto Double spring Pass Rd for 10 miles. Then turn right onto NF-117 and stay on this Rd for 6 miles, then merge onto NF-118/Upper Pahsimeroi for almost 8 miles, trailhead will be at the end of the road on the left.

properties.recarea_description: The Crosscut trail crosses several streams, passes through deep valleys carpeted with wildflowers in the spring and offers views of Horse Ranch Mountain and Steel Mountain.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.operational_hours: End of May - End of September Unless closed by snow
properties.directions: From Mountain Home travel north on State Highway 20 about 20 miles to the intersection of Forest Service (FS) road 134.  Go northwest toward Anderson Ranch Reservoir on FS road 134 about 5 miles to the intersection of FS road 113.  Go northeast about 10 miles on FS road 113, which parallels the west side of the reservoir and intersects FS road 123.  Travel north on FS road 123 for about 5 miles to the intersection of FS road 128.  On FS road 128, go south, then east for about 10 miles to Pine and a paved road. Go north about 10 miles to Featherville where the pave road ends (where FS road 156 and FS road 135 intersect).  Travel north for about 10 miles on FS road 156 to the intersection of FS road 105 and a trail directional sign.  Go northwest on FS road 105 for about 3 miles to the signed trailhead located in a prominent saddle.

properties.recarea_description: Southern access to the Gospel-Hump Wilderness and Idaho Centennial Trail #88. Trailhead for horses and pack animals.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: Approx 23 miles up the Salmon River Rd #1614 from Riggins.

properties.recarea_description: The Rainey Creek trail begins at Rainey Creek Trailhead and ends at Junction South Fork Rainey Creek Trail. The trail is open for the following uses: Off Highway Vehicles (OHV) less than or equal to 50 inches wide
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.operational_hours: Day use only: open sunrise to sunset
properties.directions: From Swan Valley go 1 mile on US-26 east. Turn left onto Rainey Creek Road. Follow Rainey Creek road for approximately 5.7 miles until you reach the trailhead

properties.recarea_description: Off Highway Vehicles (OHV) less than or equal to 50 inches wide
properties.operational_hours: Day use only: open sunrise to sunset

properties.recarea_description: This trail is popular with hikers and mountain bikers. Located close to town and not too steep, this trail is a nice hike for the entire family. Panoramic views of Sandpoint, Lake Pend Oreille and the Selkirk Mountains are offered all along the route, but the best views are near the top. Visitors will enjoy various forest settings for the entire length of the trail. Don't forget the camera, there are excellent views from this trail! USGS Quad(s): Talache View an elevation profile of the trail. View a more detailed map of the trail area.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.restrictions: Closed to all motorized vehicles yearlong.
properties.directions: From Sandpoint, take Hwy. 95 south 2 miles to Bottle Bay Road; turn left onto Bottle Bay Road and go 4.8 miles to the trailhead located on the right. Access to upper trailhead: Take Hwy. 95 south 6 miles to Sagle Road; turn left onto Sagle Road and go 6 miles to Contest Mtn. Road 2642 (located on the left at the hairpin turn); turn left onto Road 2642 and go 6 miles to the trailhead.

properties.recarea_description: Part of the Marble Creek trail system, Trail #254 features remnants of historical logging including a splash dam (one of 5 on Marble Creek), a steam donkey, and logging camp. The trail is rated as easy, but the return to the trailhead from Hobo Creek is a steep climb - be sure to take your time and rest often. This trail is open to non-motorized use only.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.closest_towns: Clarkia, ID and St Marie's, ID
properties.directions:
From Clarkia, Idaho follow Forest Road 301 to Forest Road 321. Follow Forest Road 321 to the trailhead located on the east side of the road.
From St. Marie's, Idaho follow Forest Highway 50 to Forest Road 321 at Marble Creek. Follow Forest Road 321 to the trailhead located on the east side of the road.

properties.recarea_description: One of the more remote TH's on the Payette NF, Krassel RD. This TH is located in the Monumental Draige and provides access into the Frank Church-River of No Return Wilderness and the upper portion of the Monumental Creek draige.  Just a short hike down trail from this TH you can visit the historic site of Roosevelt, which is now submerged under Roosevelt Lake.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site

properties.recarea_description: Gold Hill Trailhead is located near Potlatch ID on Forest Road 770 and provides access to approximately 13.5 miles of OHV trails and many additional miles of forest roads creating many loop opportunities for OHV users.  There is plenty of parking for trailers and two OHV loading ramps on site.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.operational_hours: Day use only; no overnight camping allowed
properties.directions: From Potlatch ID, take Onaway Road approximately 1 mile to Crane Creek Road (FSR 377), continue approximately 2 miles and take a left on Gold Creek Road (FSR 770).  Continue on FSR 770 approximately 3 miles, Gold Hill Trailhead will be on the left.

properties.recarea_description: Low Saddle Trailhead is located along the Stormy Point North Trail (#108) just north of the Hells Canyon Wilderness area. This rustic facility allows hikers and horse back riders a place to begin their visit or to pick up others coming out of the wilderness. Taking a short hike towards the canyon presents a fantastic view of Hells Canyon.
properties.information_center: Riggins- Hells Canyon National Recreation Area
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.restrictions: General rules of use and restrictions apply for this developed recreation site.Wilderness Regulations apply; within Hells Canyon Wildernes. Advisory: No motor vehicles are authorized beyond the gate and fence towards the canyon. Motorized vehicles, bicycl
properties.directions: From Riggins, Idaho travel north on Highway 95 for 1.5 miles to Forest Road 241 (Race Creek Road); Travel up Race Creek Road for 3 miles to Bean Creek Road Junction; keep right and stay on Forest Road 241 for 9 more miles to junction with Forest Road 420 (Iron Phone Junction); At Forest Road 420 junction turn left and go south for about 2 miles to Forest Road 1819 (Cold Springs Road); Travel about 9 miles on Forest Road 1819 to the trailhead.   Advisory: Many of these roads are narrow, steep and winding and are suitable for high clearance and 4x4 vehicles only.

properties.recarea_description: The West Face Trailhead is used primarily in the snow season as a snowmobile trailhead parking area. There is summertime use as a trailhead for hiking and mountain biking in the Bear Basin area.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: Travel 4.5 miles west from McCall on Highway 55 to the trailhead.  It is located on the eastern side of the highway.

properties.recarea_description: Spot Mountain Trailhead has parking suitable for a few cars. It accesses Trail #3 to Spot Mountain Lookout. There are no facilities.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: From Darby, MT travel south 4.3 miles on Highway 93, turn south (right) on the West Fork Road and proceed for approximately 14.3 miles. Turn west (right) on Forest Road 468, Nez Perce Road and travel for approximately 39 miles (Nez Perce Rd becomes Magruder Corridor.)  to the trailhead.

properties.recarea_description: This trailhead accesses Baker Lake Tr. No. 138 and the Osberg Ridgeline Tr. No. 147. Baker Lake, a pristine alpine lake less than 2 miles from the trailhead, is a perfect spot for a picnic or day hike. Or, Tr. 138 continues to connect to the Prairie Cr. and Big Smoky Cr. valleys. Osberg Ridgeline Trail is open to singletrack motorized use, including e-bikes and dirt bikes, from May 1 - Aug. 29. The trailhead is located at the end of Baker Creek Rd. No. 162 and includes a vault toilet.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site

properties.recarea_description: The Buena Vista Trailhead serves Buena Vista (#262) and Charcoal Gulch (#263) trails. Located in Idaho City adjacent to the Idaho City airstrip. In the winter Charcoal Gulch and Buena Vista become cross country ski/snowshoeing trails.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: In Idaho City, head west on W Wall St toward Commercial St for about 0.3 miles

properties.recarea_description:
The Jakie Creek/Teapot Trailhead is located along the South Fork of the Salmon River.  From the trailhead, you can travel on the west side of the river on the Cougar Creek Trail #098 that follows Jakie Creek for approximately 1 mile, then follows Cougar Creek to Cougar Lakes.
Immediately on the east side of the road is Phoebe Creek, but access to Phoebe Meadow begin at the Camp Creek Trailhead just south of this trailhead.
This trail system does loop to the south and ties into the Camp Creek Trailhead at the Camp Creek Campground (near Reed Ranch).

This is an excellent trail. Developed campgrounds located at the north end of Upper Priest Lake (Navigation Campground) and the south end of Upper Priest Lake (Plowboy Campground). The trail passes through valley and sidehill terrain. Along the trail there is an old trappers cabin, beaver ponds, abundant wildlife and scenic views. USGS Quad(s): Upper Priest Lake, Priest Lake NE, Caribou Creekview an elevation profile of the trail. View a more detailed map of the trail area.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: 1) At Nordman turn east onto Reeder Bay Road. Stay on the main road approx. 14 miles to Beaver Creek Campground. Turn right toward the campground then left uphill to the trailhead. Pull-through park available for trailers.2) North on Hwy 57, Hwy 57 turns into graveled Forest Service Rd #302 approx. 4 miles past Nordman. Travel north on Rd. #302 approx. 14 miles until it turns into Rd. #1013 at the Granite Pass junction. The road to the trailhead is on the right side, located 5.5 miles up Rd. #1013. (1 mile past the Hughes Meadows turnoff.) Stock trailer parking available.3) Trail can also be reached via Plowboy Mountain Trail #295.

properties.recarea_description: This trailhead is located just past the Big Creek Station, and is a major access point for the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness.
The Pine Gulch Trailhead includes visitor information and registration box
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.operational_hours: End of May - End of September Unless closed by snow
properties.directions: From Mtn Home travel north on Hwy 20 for 35 miles turn left onto Hwy 61 for 20 miles. Turn right onto wood creek road for 9 miles then turn right onto pine creek road.

properties.recarea_description: The Duck Lake/Hum Lake Trailhead provides access to the Twenty Mile Trail #085 and Hum Lake Trail #082 from Lick Creek Road. The hike to Duck Lake is just under 1.5 miles one way and reasoble for a wide range of ability levels. It does entrail two small stream crossings. At Duck Lake you'll find several dispersed camping sites.
properties.directions: From McCall, take Lick Creek Road approximately 18 miles. The trailhead will be on the left approximately 1.5 miles beyond Lick Creek Summit.

properties.recarea_description: Dry Saddle trailhead is one of the major trailheads accessing the Frank Church-River of No Return Wilderness lying north of the Salmon River. It provides access to many high mountain lakes along Sheep Hill Trail #575. It is only a 10-mile hike to Sheep Hill Lookout. A loading ramp is provided for stock. The 250 degree view from the trailhead is spectacular!
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: From State Highway 14, turn south onto Red River-Dixie Road #222. Follow Road #222 past Red River Ranger Station (now closed) to its junction with Nezperce Trail Road #468. Turn east onto Road #468 and follow approximately 33 miles to the trailhead.

properties.recarea_description: This area is a launch site for hangliders with picnic table and windsock at lower launch site, and a metal launch ramp at the upper launch site.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: From Mackay, ID take Hwy 93 south of Mackay 15 miles to the town of Moore. Turn left at the hanglider signs and follow them to the launch sites located on Beaver land Pass Road.

properties.recarea_description: Special attractions along the trail include five alpine lakes amid the mountains, abundant wildlife, wildflowers, and great scenic views of the mountains and valley floor. The Targhee Creek Trail is located in Grizzly Bear habitat and if camping overnight along the trail, use the bear proof storage containers provided or hang your food appropriately.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.operational_hours: Day use only; no overnight camping allowed
properties.directions: Located 16 miles north of the Island Park Ranger Station and 10 miles west of West Yellowstone, MT. Travel north 15 miles on Highway 20 then turn west on Forest Road #057. This road leads directly to the Targhee Creek Trailhead.

properties.recarea_description: Beaver Creek Trailhead provides access to Wilderness trails in the Cape Horn area.  Trail #4021 South Fork of Fall Creek is accessed from this trailhead (this trail is also referred to as Halstead Creek).
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: From Stanley, ID go 19 miles NW of Stanley on highway 21, turn north onto Forest Road #203, go .5 miles and turn left on Forest Road #008 and drive 3 miles.

properties.site_name: PALOUSE DIVIDE CROSS COUNTRY SKI TRAILHEAD
properties.recarea_name: PALOUSE DIVIDE CROSS COUNTRY SKI TRAILHEAD
properties.recarea_description: Only 42 miles north of the college town of Moscow, in north central Idaho, skiers, skate skiers and snowshoers alike will find groomed as well as backcountry trails.  Known for its beautiful landscape and spiraling evergreen trees reaching high into the sky, the 18 miles of winter trails range from easy to intermediate in skill level required, making the Palouse Divide Nordic Ski Area ideal for beginners as well as those with more experience.  A Idaho Department of Recreation Park n' Ski pass is required for parking from November 15th to April 30th.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: From Potlatch ID travel north on Highway 6/Whitepine Drive for 22 miles.  The parking area is at the top of the Palouse Divide on FSR 377.

properties.recarea_description: Nez Perce Pass Trailhead has adequate parking for both cars and trailer. It offers access to trail #16, the Selway Bitterroot Wilderness and the Frank Church Wilderness. Facilities include a vault toilet and hitching rails.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: From Darby, MT travel south 4.3 miles on Highway 93, turn south on the West Fork Road and proceed for approximately 14.3 miles. Turn west (right) on Forest Road 468, Nez Perce Road and travel for approximately 16.1 miles to the trailhead.

properties.recarea_description: One accessible camping spot, with accessible toilet, located in open sagebrush. The trailhead accesses 3 trails: Waterfall accessible trail (4344), Fall Creek (4045) and Moose Lake (4068).
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: From Mackay, ID take US Highway 93 16 miles north of Mackay to the Trail Creek Road. Turn left on the Trail Creek Road. Follow this road 18 miles to the Copper Basin Road. Turn left on the Road #135. Follow this road 2 miles to the Wildhorse Creek Road (#136). Stay to the right on the Wildhorse Creek Road. Follow the Wildhorse Creek Road 3.5 miles to the Fall Creek Road (#503). Turn left on the Fall Creek Road and follow it to the trailhead.

properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site

properties.recarea_description: Just 50 miles east of Moscow, Idaho, visitors will find The Elk Creek Falls Recreation Area, home to the Elk Creek Falls National Recreation Trail, with one of the most scenic waterfalls in the state of Idaho. Three separate waterfalls totaling over 140 feet carve a beautiful canyon filled with mesmerizing columnar basaltic formations... with amenities such as restrooms, picnic tables, pedestal grills and trailhead information all accessible by a developed Forest Service trail... Elk Creek Falls awaits you!
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.operational_hours: Day use only; no overnight camping allowed
properties.directions: From Moscow, Idaho, travel east on Hwy. 8, passing through Troy, Deary and Bovill.  Approximately 11 miles past the town of Bovill will be signs for Elk Creek Falls Recreation Area.  Turn right on FS Road 1452 (gravel road), in a couple of miles road leads to the recreation area parking lot.

properties.recarea_description: An unimproved trailhead providing access to Kay-Trapper Trail #147, and Kay Creek Trail #151.
properties.important_info: Forest Service Road 9705 is not suitable for full-sized vehicles.

properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site

properties.recarea_description: Take the opportunity to travel the lovely White Pine Scenic Byway, Idaho 6, north from the quaint town of Harvard, Idaho for just over 7 miles to visit this special site. Named after an enormous, 600 year old white pine that has since been cut down due to disease (but still resides in the site!).  The trailhead offers restrooms, picnic tables and access to many mile of motorized single track trail , including the National Recreation Trail 224A, the East Fork Meadows Creek Trail.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.operational_hours: Day use only; no overnight camping allowed
properties.water_availability: Yes, drinking water is available from a hand pump
properties.directions: Travel north on Highway 6/Whitepine Drive, 7.7 miles from Harvard, Idaho.

properties.recarea_description: This trailhead provides access for the Marsh Creek Trail #4237, the Bear Valley-Marsh Creek Trail #4010, and the Middle Fork Trail #4001.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: From Stanley, Idaho travel 17 miles NW on Hwy 21.  Turn right on Lola Creek Rd/40083 for approximately 2 miles, trailhead is at the end of the road.

properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
No fees are required for this site

properties.site_name: MIDDLE FORK PAYETTE RIVER/WET FOOT TRAILHEAD
properties.recarea_name: Middle Fork Payette River/Wet Foot Trailhead
properties.recarea_description: MIDDLE FORK PAYETTE RIVER/WET FOOT TRAILHEAD (Trailhead)
properties.public_site_name: Middle Fork Payette River/Wet Foot Trail

properties.recarea_description: This trailhead is on the edge of Forest Road #257, and provides access to the Grass Mountain Trail. It is a leisurely two mile hike to Grass Mountain Lakes. Spur trails provide access to Coffee Cup Lake, Frog Lake, and Morgan Lake.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: This trailhead is about 45 minutes from McCall. To reach the trailhead, take Highway 55 west out of McCall for four miles. Turn right onto the Goose Lake Road (tiol Forest Road 257) for about 18 miles.

properties.recarea_description: Lake Fork Trailhead provides access to Lake Fork First Bridge Trail #339. This pleasant trail is shaded and cool, a good place to gather huckleberries.  There is little change in elevation along the trail and it is a scenic mountain bike ride. It is about a 30 minute drive east of McCall (11 miles).
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
No fees are required for this site
properties.operational_hours: Day use only; no overnight camping allowed

properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.operational_hours: Day use only: open sunrise to sunset
properties.directions: From Driggs, ID drive to Alta WY on E Ski Hill Rd. Continue on Alta Rd/Targhee Rd. Turn right on Teton Canyon Rd. Go approximately 0.7 miles

properties.recarea_description: Visitors will travel the scenic Magruder Road Corridor to reach 14 Mile Trailhead, which offers a starting point for hikers and pack trains to reach the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness via Trail 501-the Cache Creek Trail and Trail 580-the Boston Mountain Trail. Along with 2 camp pads, an unloading ramp, hitch rails, stock feeders and a restroom, visitors can also enjoy three interpretive panels with descriptions of Frank Church and information on the Frank Church-River of No Return Wilderness.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: From State Highway 14, turn south onto Red River-Dixie Road #222. Follow Road #222 past Red River Ranger Station (now closed) to its junction with the Nez Perce Trail Road #468. Turn east onto Road #468 and follow approximately 14 miles to the campground and trailhead.

properties.recarea_description: This is a very popular and well-used trail system just minutes from Coeur d'Alene and Hayden, Idaho that winds through large trees and grassy understory near the shores of Hayden Lake. The trail system is divided between user groups with one side for hikers and the other for equestrians. The trail is also open in the winter for cross-country skiing and snow shoeing, but motorized use is never allowed. The total distance is about 6 miles with a cumulative elevation gain of about 300 feet. Thanks to a 2019 Eagle Scout project, the trail now has 14 benches, an amphitheater, and a picnic table.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.closest_towns: Hayden, ID and Coeur d'Alene, ID
properties.directions: From Coeur d'Alene, head north on Highway 95 for about 7 miles. Turn right onto Lancaster Road and continue for 3.5 miles. Turn right onto English Point Road. The trailhead will be on your immediate left.

properties.recarea_description: The Twenty Mile trailhead is accessed via Warren Wagon Road and features a horse unloading ramp, hitching rails, and toilet. There is a large parking area with sufficient space for trailers.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: Take Warren Wagon Road north for 18 miles. The trailhead will be on the right.

properties.recarea_description: The Horse Heaven Trail is about 10 miles west of Atlanta, near Swanholm Peak, and is a part of the Black Warrior/ Swanholm/Horse Heaven trail system. The trail connects Black Warrior and Horse Heaven Trails.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: From Boise, Idaho, travel State Highway 21, northeast to Idaho City, Idaho. Turn off State Highway 21 onto Forest Service (FS) Road 384 at Edna Creek (18 miles past Idaho City). Follow FS Road 384 for 13.5 miles to the North Fork Boise River and FS Road 327. Turn upriver (left) on FS Road 327 and cross the North Fork Boise River by bridge just below Deer Park Cabin. Continue on FS Road 327 for another 2 miles to Horse Heaven Creek and Trailhead.

properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site

properties.recarea_description: The Box Lake Trail is steep and difficult but worth the effort. The route gains 800' in the first mile. The 3.4 mile segment from the Box Lake Trailhead to the south end of Box Lake is desigted non-motorized. The 1.8 mile segment from the south end of Box Lake to the Crestline Trail #109 is open to two-wheel motorized use.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: From McCall, follow Lick Creek Road approximately 15 miles to the trailhead.

properties.recarea_description: Kim Creek Saddle Trailhead has adequate parking for cars. It offers access to trail #26 and #89 and the Frank Church Wilderness. Facilities include an old wooden outhouse, and hitching rails.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.water_availability: No, drinking water is not provided
properties.directions: From Darby, MT travel south 4.3 miles on Highway 93, turn south on the West Fork Road and proceed for approximately 14.3 miles.  Turn west (right) on Forest Road 468, Nez Perce Road and travel for approximately  35 miles (Nez Perce Rd becomes Magruder Corridor.) Turn west (left) at Magruder Corridor Nez Perce Trail Rd. and continue for 6.5 miles to the trailhead.

properties.recarea_description: Lick Creek Trailhead has a vault toilet, but no potable water.

Greenhorn Trailhead is one of the busiest motorized trailheads on the Ketchum Ranger District. All designated trails in the Greenhorn drainage are open to singletrack motorized use, including dirt bikes and e-bikes. Area trails are also popular with stock users. Loop opportunities from the trailhead are almost limitless - The map kiosk at the trailhead can help you plan your route. Other amenities at the trailhead include a vault toilet, picnic shelter, and fire ring.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site

properties.recarea_description: This is one of the most beautiful trails on the Sandpoint Ranger District and is popular with hikers and mountain bikers. Gentle grades, wildflowers and excellent views make this trail suitable for the entire family. Constructed by volunteers and dedicated to the memory of Brent Jake Jacobson who gave his life in the line of duty as a Forest Service law enforcement officer. This trail ends at Green Bay Campground on Lake Pend Oreille. There is a toilet, picnic tables and fire grills. USGS Quad(s): Packsaddle NW. View an elevation profile of the trail. View a more detailed map of the trail area.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.restrictions: Closed to all motorized vehicles yearlong.
properties.directions: From Sandpoint, take Hwy. 95 south 6 miles to Sagle Road; turn left onto Sagle Road and go 9 miles to Garfield Bay; turn left on the first road past the public boat launch and go about a quarter mile to Mineral Point Road 532; turn right onto Road 532 and follow signs to the trailhead. Road 532 also provides access to Green Bay Campground Road 2672 and Lost Lake Trail 81.

properties.recarea_description: Access to Upper Hazard Lake from the north. Upper Hazard/Hard Creek Basin Trail #169 is open to motorcycles. The area is popular for hiking, mountain bikes and motorcycles. The trailhead is just south of the Hazard Lake Campground.
properties.directions: This trailhead is about an hour from McCall. To reach the trailhead, take Highway 55 west out of McCall for four miles. Turn right onto the Goose Lake Road (tiol Forest Road 257) for about 20 miles.

properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site

properties.activity_type_list: HIKING & WALKING | HORSEBACK RIDING | MOTORCYCLES & SCOOTERS
properties.recarea_description: Off Highway Vehicles (OHV) less than or equal to 50 inches wide
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.operational_hours: Day use only: open sunrise to sunset
properties.directions: From Heise head south east on E Heise road for 1.3 miles. Continue straight onto E Kelly Canyon Ro for 3.5 miles. Turn right on Forest Rd 218 and follow for 10.5 miles. Turn right on Forest Road 651 and follow for 1.9 miles until you reach your destition.

properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site

properties.recarea_description: This trail system includes trails #401 Frank Brown, #407 Snoose Creek, #431 Driveway, and #478 Blue Ridge. These are accessible by a pack bridge on the South Fork of the Clearwater River along Highway 14. Ruby Creek is the headwaters of the Secech River and other creeks such as Summit Creek are near by.  The trailhead provides access Willow Basket Creek Trail #141, and is an access route to Loon Lake; the primary route to Loon Lake is Via the Loon Lake Trail #081 that begins at the Loon Lake Trailhead near Chinook Campground.
Ruby 1-Trail #173 and Ruby 2-Trail #174 are perfect day hiking trails, and OHV riding.  The Willow Basket Trail #148 is a motorized double loop off of the Willow Basket Creek Trail #141.  It is just over 2.5 miles long, a and is open to ATV Trail Riding.

properties.recarea_description: The Snow Peak WMA is dedicated to wildlife management and is co-managed with the Idaho Department of Fish and Game (IDFG). It is bounded by Trail 40 and Road 395 in the south, Little North Fork Clearwater River and Spotted Louis Creek in the west, and Road 201 in the north and east. Ownership in the Spotted Louis, Canyon and Buck Creek drainages is in a checkerboard pattern with every other section belonging to the State of Idaho. Elevations range from 2,600 feet along the Little North Fork Clearwater River, to 6,760 feet at Snow Peak Lookout. The area encompasses a scenic and ecologically diverse area that provides recreationists the opportunity to hunt, fish and enjoy nature with a high degree of solitude. Mountain goats are frequently seen in the area.

properties.recarea_description: The Bear Gulch/Mesa Falls trail system is one of the most scenic anywhere in Idaho, particularly because the ski trails cruise along the rim overlooking both Upper and Lower Mesa Falls. Views of the Teton Mountain Range are possible on a clear day. It's a 9.1-mile round-trip trek to the Upper Falls (where the water falls 110 feet), but well worth the effort for the strong and hardy. Shorter loops of 3.9 miles or 5.9 are available closer to the trailhead. The trailhead and a short section of the ski trail are shared use areas with snowmobiles.

This trailhead also includes an interpretive site with information on history and fish.

The route to Snowslide Lake begins on the east side of Lick Creek Road. The trail is steep and rocky, with an elevation gain of about 1,200' to the lake. The area around Snowslide Lake is ringed by mature trees, granite walls, and steep slopes, untouched by recent fire activity. There are several dispersed campsites around the lake. Beyond the lake Trail #104 trail splits at the intersection for Maki Lake Trail #135 (beware that trail #135 is difficult to find) and follows the East Fork of Lake Fork Creek to the Lake Fork Campground. It is necessary to ford Lake Fork to access the trail to Snowslide Lake, so this hike is not recommended in early spring due to high water.

The trail follows the road going past the Upper Pittsburg Picnic Area and goes about 6 miles to Kirkwood Ranch and beyond. From Riggins, Idaho head north on Highway 95 for about 27 miles to Old Highway 95 at mile marker 222 (sign indicates Pittsburg Landing and Hammer Creek Recreation Site); Turn left on Old Highway 95 and go about 1 mile to the bridge crossing the Salmon River; Turn left and cross the bridge; Immediately after the bridge turn left on the Deer Creek Road (also known as Forest Road 493); Travel on the Deer Creek Road for 16.5 miles to Forest Road 493A; Turn left on Forest Road 493A and go 1.3 miles to trailhead parking area. The trail follows the road going past the Upper Pittsburg Picnic Area and goes about 6 miles to Kirkwood Ranch and beyond.  Advisory: The Deer Creek Road (Forest Road 493) is a steep, narrow winding paved gravel road.

properties.recarea_description: Warm Springs Trailhead serves as access to the Selway Bitterroot Wilderness and to the Jerry Johnson Hot Springs. It is located at  MP 152 on the famous Northwest Passage Scenic Byway and All American Road (US Highway 12) along the Lochsa Wild and Scenic River, approximately an hour and half from Kooskia, ID or an hour from Lolo, MT.  This area is known for its panoramic views of the Selway Bitterroot Wilderness and spectacular wildflower displays, and is a perfect spot for horseback riding, hiking and hot spring enjoyment. Two parking spaces are provided: one is for stock use.
properties.fee_description: No fees are required for this site
properties.directions: Located at Milepost 152 along US. Highway 12.

properties.recarea_description: Open to ATVs. Part of the Peewee/Steep Creek trail system. The trail system is a series of interconnected loops and each trail can be accessed from several different points. Some loops gain elevations that view the Priest Lake and Pend Orielle River Valleys. Some sections are located on the old road bed while others are steep and rocky.USGS Quad(s): Quartz MountainView an elevation profile of the trail.View a more detailed map of the trail area.

properties.recarea_description: The Windy Saddle Trailhead is the main access point into the Hells Canyon Wilderness from Idaho. Located on the saddle going to Seven Devils basin or up to Heaven's Gate Lookout, the area offers a great view of the Seven Devils mountain range and the Hells Canyon area. This site provides access to Seven Devils Trail #124 and Sheep Creek Trail #53 which enter Hells Canyon Wilderness.

properties.directions: From Riggins, Idaho travel south on Highway 95 for 1.3 miles to Seven Devils Road (becomes Forest Road 517); Turn right on Seven Devils Road and go 17 miles to trailhead and horse camp road junction; Take a left at the road junction then turn right into the trailhead entrance.   ADVISORY: Forest Road 517 is very steep, and narrow. Low clearance vehicles, RVs and vehicles pulling trailers are not recommended or advised. Use caution when traveling the upper sections of this road. The road can also be slippery when wet or frozen and is not recommended for trailers in the late fall and winter.

properties.recarea_description: The Heaven's Gate Trailhead is located below Heaven's Gate Viewpoint near the Hells Canyon Wilderness. Visitors to the site can enjoy a short hike up to the fire lookout viewpoint on the Heaven's Gate National Recreation Trail, or walk along the northern portion of the Boise Trail (#101) and look down into Hells Canyon.  The Boise Trail #101 provides access to Hells Canyon Wilderness via the Old Timer Trail #110 junction north of Heaven's Gate Trailhead.
